title: Lecture III — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961) | Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: The first lunar passage confronts the dead with their moral character and the primeval teachers.
interpretation_qualification: GA 108 separately describes the period of releasing desires. An exact concordance of all its phases with GA 231 remains open.

title: Lecture III — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: Understanding of what had previously been perceived starts to develop as the dead encounter the Third Hierarchy.
interpretation_qualification: This is an experience of several ranks, while GA 110 draws a single boundary marker for Archangeloi.

title: Lecture III — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: The dead encounter cosmic love in Venus existence. The sphere works especially on the will.
interpretation_qualification: Steiner describes the response as depending on capacities brought from life on Earth.

process: Music of the spheres | Outward journey after death
title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: The dead experience cosmic harmony in the Sun sphere.
interpretation_qualification: GA 231 III also associates this solar stage with feeling and the Second Hierarchy.

process: Cosmic speech | Outward journey after death
title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: Cosmic music becomes cosmic speech in the Mars region.
interpretation_qualification: GA 228 gives a parallel Mars speech motif in a different frame.

process: Cosmic thought | Outward journey after death
title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: Jupiter’s spiritual beings guard and radiate cosmic thoughts, which the human being encounters.
interpretation_qualification: This is part of the metamorphosis leading toward the head germ of another incarnation.

process: Cosmic memory | Outward journey after death
title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: The person encounters the planetary system’s cosmic memory in the Saturn sphere.
interpretation_qualification: Compare the Saturn memory description in GA 228.

title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: On return through Saturn, cosmic memory becomes the germ of the future human faculty of memory.
interpretation_qualification: Steiner distinguishes outward experience and return transformation.

title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: On return through Jupiter, perceived cosmic thoughts are transformed into a germ of earthly thinking.
interpretation_qualification: The change is linked to the spiritual germ of the head.

title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: On return through Mars, participation in the cosmic Word is linked to the germ of human speech.
interpretation_qualification: The same paragraph also names chest and limb germs.

title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: Steiner assigns the addition of new spiritual limb and breast-system germs to the Mars passage.
interpretation_qualification: He explicitly places this on a spiritual level.

title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: Steiner jointly places implantation of additional organ germs at the passages through Venus and Mercury.
interpretation_qualification: He gives no organ-by-organ assignment here.

title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: Mercury and Venus are both named in the passage on other organ germs.
interpretation_qualification: This does not independently prove that Mercury supplies lung germs.

title: Lecture IV — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: The account puts the return lunar passage alongside the earthly interval between conception and birth.
interpretation_qualification: This is an esoteric parallel with embryonic development.

title: Lecture IV — GA 239. Karmic Relationships VII (1973)
paraphrase: Steiner characterizes Saturn’s way of shaping karma through a relation to the past and intense effects in the soul.
interpretation_qualification: GA 239’s historical incarnation identifications are claims of its lecture context.

paraphrase: Steiner places Exusiai, Dynamis and Kyriotetes in the Sun sphere in accounts of the interval between lives.

title: Lecture III — GA 239. Karmic Relationships VII (1973)
paraphrase: Steiner argues that people carry effects of earlier historical conditions into later epochs through reincarnation.
interpretation_qualification: The claim belongs to his esoteric account of history.

title: Lecture III — GA 231. Supersensible Man (1961)
paraphrase: Sun-sphere forces act particularly on what appears on Earth as feeling.
interpretation_qualification: GA 209 associates feeling with rhythm in embodied life through a different explanatory route.

title: Knowledge of reincarnation and karma through thought-exercises — GA 135. Reincarnation and Karma, Their Significance in Modern Culture (1977)
paraphrase: The lecture proposes imagining a person whose aims and faculties correspond to events that appear accidental.
interpretation_qualification: The exercise is an approach Steiner proposes to karma, not a way to establish a particular incarnation historically.
